title: High-resolution TVD, ENO and WENO reconstruction

items.title: Finite-volume MUSCL, nodal ENO2 and WENO5 reconstruction conventions
items.statement:
Let $h>0$, let $I_i=[ih,(i+1)h)$, let $x_i=(i+\tfrac12)h$ be its center, and write $x_{i+1/2}=(i+1)h$ and $x_{i-1/2}=ih$ for its right and left faces. A **cell average** of a locally integrable scalar function $u$ is $U_i=h^{-1}\int_{I_i}u(x)\,dx$. The cells are half-open only to form a partition; the choice of endpoint representatives does not change an integral.

Here **MUSCL/minmod** means the piecewise-linear reconstruction with the limiter defined next; **nodal ENO2** means the two-stencil quadratic selector defined below; and **cell-average WENO5-JS/WENO-Z** means the three-candidate reconstructions with the normalized nonlinear weights displayed below. These names specify the constructions and do not, by themselves, assert an accuracy or stability property.

For real $a,b$, define
$$\operatorname{minmod}(a,b)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{sgn}(a)\min(|a|,|b|),&ab>0,\\0,&ab\le0.\end{cases}$$
The **MUSCL/minmod reconstruction** assigns the cell slope $s_i=h^{-1}\operatorname{minmod}(U_i-U_{i-1},U_{i+1}-U_i)$ and the two face states $U_{i-1/2}^{+,M}=U_i-hs_i/2$ and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,M}=U_i+hs_i/2$. Here $+$ denotes a trace from the right cell and $-$ a trace from the left cell.

For separate **nodal** data $V_j=u(y_j)$ at $y_j=jh$, define the second divided difference by $[y_a,y_b,y_c]V=(((V_c-V_b)/(y_c-y_b))-((V_b-V_a)/(y_b-y_a)))/(y_c-y_a)$. At the face $y_{i+1/2}=(i+\tfrac12)h$, set $d_L=|[y_{i-1},y_i,y_{i+1}]V|$ and $d_R=|[y_i,y_{i+1},y_{i+2}]V|$. Choose the left triple when $d_L\le d_R$ and otherwise choose the right triple. For the selected triple $(y_a,y_b,y_c)$ define its Newton quadratic by
$$P_{a,b,c}(y)=V_a+\frac{V_b-V_a}{y_b-y_a}(y-y_a)+[y_a,y_b,y_c]V\,(y-y_a)(y-y_b).$$
The **nodal ENO2 face value** is $P_{a,b,c}(y_{i+1/2})$. This nodal interpolation branch is distinct from the cell-average WENO branch below.

For cell averages $U_{i-2},\ldots,U_{i+2}$, define the left-biased WENO5 candidate face functionals
$$p_0=(2U_{i-2}-7U_{i-1}+11U_i)/6,\qquad p_1=(-U_{i-1}+5U_i+2U_{i+1})/6,\qquad p_2=(2U_i+5U_{i+1}-U_{i+2})/6.$$
Define the Jiang–Shu indicators
$$\beta_0=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-2}-2U_{i-1}+U_i)^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-2}-4U_{i-1}+3U_i)^2,$$
$$\beta_1=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-1}-2U_i+U_{i+1})^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-1}-U_{i+1})^2,\qquad \beta_2=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_i-2U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2+\tfrac14(3U_i-4U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2.$$
Fix a positive parameter $\epsilon_0$ with the same units as each $\beta_k$, independently of $h$, and ideal weights $(d_0,d_1,d_2)=(1/10,6/10,3/10)$. If $u$ is nondimensionalized, $\epsilon_0$ is a fixed positive number. The **WENO-JS weights** and left face value are $\alpha_k^J=d_k/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k)^2$, $\omega_k^J=\alpha_k^J/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^J$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,J}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Jp_k$. For the **WENO-Z comparison**, use the fifth-order $p=2$ weights: with $\tau_5=|\beta_0-\beta_2|$, set $\alpha_k^Z=d_k[1+(\tau_5/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k))^2]$, $\omega_k^Z=\alpha_k^Z/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^Z$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,Z}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Zp_k$. All denominators are positive because $\epsilon_0>0$ and every $\beta_k$ is a sum of squares. The right face state is obtained by reflection about that face: replace each stencil value $U_k$ in the displayed left formula by $U_{2i+1-k}$.

For scalar linear advection $u_t+a u_x=0$, a **direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update** uses $\nu=a\Delta t/h$, the flux $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{-,M}$ when $a\ge0$ and $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{+,M}$ when $a<0$, and $U_i^{n+1}=U_i^n-(\Delta t/h)(F_{i+1/2}-F_{i-1/2})$. The total variation of a sequence is $\operatorname{TV}(U)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}|U_{i+1}-U_i|$ when the sum is finite; **TVD** means that this quantity does not increase in one update.

For a vector system whose flux Jacobian at an interface is diagonalizable as $A=R\Lambda R^{-1}$ with real diagonal $\Lambda$, a **characteristic-wise reconstruction** applies a chosen scalar reconstruction to the components of $R^{-1}U$ and maps the reconstructed vector back by $R$. This definition alone gives no TVD or stability result for systems.

items.title: A monotone linear one-step advection scheme cannot be second order at noninteger CFL
items.statement:
Let $a
e0$, $h>0$ and $\Delta t>0$, and put $
u=a\Delta t/h$. Fix a noninteger $
u$. Consider a finite-stencil, translation-invariant linear one-step scheme
$$U_j^{n+1}=\sum_{\ell=-r}^{r}c_\ell U_{j+\ell}^n$$
with real coefficients that may depend on the fixed $
u$ but are independent of $h$, $j$ and $n$. Assume the scheme is conservative, is consistent with $u_t+a u_x=0$, and is second-order accurate in the local truncation sense. For these fixed coefficients, second-order consistency requires exact matching of the constant, linear and quadratic Taylor moments for the one-step translation. If the update is monotone in the componentwise order on grid sequences, then these assumptions are inconsistent. Thus at a noninteger Courant number no such linear monotone scheme can be second order.

references.title: Randall J. LeVeque, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, full textbook
references.locator: Ch. 16 §16.1, Theorem 16.1, printed pp. 174–175 (PDF pp. 187–188): a linear monotonicity-preserving method is at most first order.

items.title: The selected nodal ENO2 quadratic reconstructs the face to third order
items.statement:
Let $h>0$, let $y_j=jh$, and let $u\in C^3([y_{i-1},y_{i+2}])$ with $M:=\sup|u'''|<\infty$. Form the nodal ENO2 value at $y_{i+1/2}$ by the rule in [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]]. Then
$$|U^{ENO2}_{i+1/2}-u(y_{i+1/2})|\le Mh^3/16.$$
The conclusion holds for either selected triple, so it includes the left-tie case.

items.title: The WENO5 ideal linear weights reproduce quartics at the right face
items.statement: Let $h>0$, let $I_j=[jh,(j+1)h)$, and let $x_{i+1/2}=(i+1)h$. For $u\in C^5$ on the union of cells $I_{i-2},\ldots,I_{i+2}$, let $p_0,p_1,p_2$ be the cell-average functionals in [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]]. Each candidate reproduces every polynomial of degree at most two exactly at $x_{i+1/2}$. The ideal combination $p_{opt}=p_0/10+3p_1/5+3p_2/10$ reproduces every polynomial of degree at most four and satisfies $|p_{opt}-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le (23/15)(3^5/5!)\,\sup|u^{(5)}|\,h^5$. Each candidate separately satisfies $|p_k-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le15\sup|u'''|h^3$.

items.title: MUSCL/minmod face states are second order on smooth monotone data
items.statement:
Let $u\in C^2$ on a neighborhood of a cell and its two neighbors, and suppose $|u'(x)|\ge c>0$ there. Let $U_j$ be the averages of $u$ over uniform cells of width $h$, centered at $x_j=x_0+jh$. For sufficiently small $h$, the MUSCL/minmod face states of [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]] satisfy
$$|U_i+hs_i/2-u(x_i+h/2)|\le C h^2,\qquad |U_i-hs_i/2-u(x_i-h/2)|\le C h^2,$$
where $C$ depends only on $c$ and a bound for $|u''|$ on the stated neighborhood.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 31–35: cell-centered piecewise-linear MUSCL reconstruction and minmod selection.

items.title: Direct forward-Euler MUSCL/minmod is TVD under the sharp two-thirds CFL bound
items.statement:
Let $h>0$, $\Delta t\ge0$, $a\in\mathbb R$, and $\mu=|a|\Delta t/h$. Use the direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update for scalar linear advection from [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]], with the stated MUSCL/minmod reconstruction and no time predictor; write $U^+$ for the sequence after one such update. The data are either a real bi-infinite sequence with finite discrete total variation
$$\operatorname{TV}(U)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}|U_i-U_{i-1}|<\infty,$$
or a real $N$-periodic sequence, for an integer $N\ge1$, with
$$\operatorname{TV}_N(U)=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}|U_i-U_{i-1}|,$$
where periodic indices are taken modulo $N$. If $0\le\mu\le2/3$, one update satisfies $\operatorname{TV}(U^+)\le\operatorname{TV}(U)$ in the bi-infinite case and $\operatorname{TV}_N(U^+)\le\operatorname{TV}_N(U)$ in the periodic case.

The constant $2/3$ is sharp within the original range $0\le\mu\le1$: for every $2/3<\mu\le1$ there are finite-support data of variation $2$ whose updated variation is $3\mu>2$. For every period $N\ge7$, the same witness periodized with period $N$ has the same strict increase.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 31–35: equation (3.1.2) is the direct MUSCL update, equation (3.3.1) is minmod, and equation (3.3.8) gives the sufficient CFL restriction. The variation estimate, signed-velocity reduction and sharpness are proved locally.

items.title: The specified direct MUSCL/minmod flux update is not TVD at CFL one
items.statement: The direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update in [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]] is TVD for every scalar grid sequence whenever $|a|\Delta t/h\le1$.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §3.3, PDF pp. 32–35, especially condition (3.3.8): the minmod MUSCL update requires an additional CFL restriction; the local finite data below directly refute the PE02 CFL-one assertion.

items.title: Fixed-epsilon WENO-JS and WENO-Z face reconstructions are fifth order
items.statement:
Let $u\in C^5$ on the five-cell stencil, let $\sup|u'''|<\infty$ and $\sup|u^{(5)}|<\infty$, and let $\epsilon_0>0$ be fixed independently of $h$. For the cell-average WENO-JS and WENO-Z states in [[def-na-high-resolution-reconstruction]], there is a constant $C$ independent of sufficiently small $h$ such that
$$|U_{i+1/2}^{-,J}-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le Ch^5,\qquad |U_{i+1/2}^{-,Z}-u(x_{i+1/2})|\le Ch^5.$$
The same result holds for the reflected right states.

title: High-resolution TVD, ENO and WENO reconstruction — Examples

items.title: Minmod clips the slope at a smooth quadratic maximum
items.statement: For $u(x)=1-(x-h/2)^2$ and cells $I_j=[jh,(j+1)h)$, the cell average in the central cell $I_0$ is $U_0=1-h^2/12$ and its two neighbors have $U_{-1}=U_1=1-13h^2/12$. The minmod slope in the central cell is zero, so the reconstruction clips the central slope at the smooth maximum.

items.title: Unlimited centered reconstruction creates new extrema on a step
items.statement: An unlimited centered-slope reconstruction with the reconstructed upwind forward-Euler update is TVD and range-preserving for every scalar grid sequence whenever $|a|\Delta t/h\le1$.

items.title: MUSCL and WENO reconstruct a translating affine profile exactly
items.statement: Let $I_i=[ih,(i+1)h)$, $x_i=(i+\tfrac12)h$, and $u(x,t)=x-at$ for a fixed $a\in\mathbb R$. On this affine profile, both the minmod MUSCL reconstruction and each of the three normalized WENO5 reconstructions give the exact upwind face value; the corresponding conservative forward-Euler update advances every cell average exactly by one time step.

items.title: A first-order critical point exposes WENO-JS epsilon scaling
items.statement: Work in nondimensional coordinates with $u(x)=x^2+x^3$ and reconstruct the face $x=0$, the interface between cells $I_{-1}$ and $I_0$. This is a first-order critical point: $u'(0)=0$ and $u''(0)=2$. If the WENO-JS parameter is scaled as $\epsilon_h=h^4$, the cell-average face state has error $\frac{54}{95}h^4+O(h^5)$, so this branch is fourth order at the face. With the fixed $\epsilon_0>0$ of [[thm-na-weno-js-fixed-epsilon-fifth-order-reconstruction]], the theorem's fifth-order branch applies; with the same $\epsilon_h$, the WENO-Z comparison has error $O(h^6)$ on this polynomial.

references.title: Andrew K. Henrick, Tariq D. Aslam and Joseph M. Powers, Mapped weighted essentially non-oscillatory schemes: Achieving optimal order near critical points
references.locator: §§4.2–4.5, printed pp. 552–554: the WENO-JS order depends on epsilon and resolution at critical points. The source analyzes finite-difference fluxes; the cell-average face calculation here is performed explicitly.

references.title: Guang-Shan Jiang and Chi-Wang Shu, Efficient Implementation of Weighted ENO Schemes

items.title: Positive-state Burgers shock and the monotone finite-volume baseline
items.statement: For $f(u)=u^2/2$ and $u_0(x)=1$ for $x<0$, $u_0(x)=0$ for $x>0$, the entropy shock moves right at speed $1/2$. For states $a,b\in[0,1]$, define the positive-state Burgers Godunov flux by $F_G(a,b)=\min_{v\in[a,b]}f(v)$ when $a\le b$ and $F_G(a,b)=\max_{v\in[b,a]}f(v)$ when $a>b$. Since $f$ is increasing on $[0,1]$, both cases give $F_G(a,b)=a^2/2$. Minmod slopes vanish for the initial step, so the first MUSCL flux update is the first-order Godunov update; the batch-29 monotone finite-volume theorem applies to its mesh-refined baseline under Countable Choice and the stated CFL conditions.
